name: Kasa KS200M (US)

matter.note: Neither the product page nor the datasheet mentions Matter; no CSA listing was checked.

apple_home.note: The KS200M page and datasheet do not mention Apple Home. (The non-motion KS200 page does mention it.)

google_home.note: Listed as working with Google Assistant.

alexa.note: Listed as working with Amazon Alexa.

home_assistant.note: No official Home Assistant page naming the KS200M was checked.

hubRequired.note: The datasheet says no hub is required; it connects straight to home Wi-Fi.

localControl.note: TP-Link does not state what works without internet.

switchForm.note: Replaces a standard single-pole light switch and has a built-in motion sensor (up to 25 ft).

dimmer.note: TP-Link mentions setting "brightness levels" but never calls it a dimmer; the datasheet gives only on/off load ratings (600 W incandescent, 1/6 HP motor). Left unconfirmed.

neutralRequired.note: The datasheet says a neutral wire in the wall box is required, in a standard box at least 2 in deep.

gangs.note: Single-pole only; not compatible with 3-way or multi-way wiring. Rated 120 V, 600 W incandescent or 1/6 HP motor.

summary: TP-Link lists the Kasa KS200M for Alexa, Google Assistant and SmartThings, with no hub needed. It's a US single-pole wall switch with a built-in motion sensor (up to 25 ft) that joins 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi directly. It needs a neutral wire and won't work in 3-way setups. Apple Home and Matter aren't mentioned for this model.
caveats: Needs a neutral wire in the wall box.
Single-pole only; no 3-way or multi-way wiring.
Apple Home and Matter support are not stated.
